title: Forgel Code: interactive agent client instead of a command wrapper
request: The Forgel Code client stops being only a set of one-shot, argument-driven wrappers. Opened without arguments it starts an interactive session in which the owner describes work in plain language, reads the agent's answers, follows the plan and the progress of tasks and releases, and accepts work or sends it back with remarks without leaving the session. Adopting a repository, creating a project, secrets and configuration stay explicit. One-shot scripted usage and its machine-readable output remain unchanged, and the client stays thin: the model, the sandbox, independent checks, review and releases stay in the engine. The requirements below follow the existing feature document named by the owner and the client's documented contract; they are behaviour, not implementation.

audit.summary: The interactive session is broadly implemented and its test suite passes, but the release still violates security and compatibility requirements: redaction leaks secrets for French/Spanish labels and for quoted labels followed by unquoted values; sensitive-operation refusal is not localized; and `--help` output changed despite the one-shot output contract. A README statement also contradicts action resolution.

findings.issue: The redactor recognizes only English secret words and Russian stems (`SECRET_WORDS`, `SECRET_STEMS`). The session now speaks French and Spanish, but replies such as `mot de passe : hunter2`, `clé: ...` or `contraseña: hunter2` are not recognized and are displayed unchanged, and can also be retained in state or error text. This violates the requirement that masking hold in every language the session speaks and the release's no-secret-on-screen requirement.
findings.suggestion: Extend label recognition with French/Spanish secret terms, including multi-word `mot de passe`, and add direct, session-level and retained-state tests for these forms; ensure the same redactor is applied on every engine display path.

findings.issue: In `_quoted_binding`, after a quoted label and whitespace, a bare next token returns `None` unless a colon/equals separator or another quote follows. Thus `'token' hunter2` and a double-quoted label followed by an unquoted value are never masked, failing the quoted-label requirement for a label followed by an unquoted value and leaving a credential visible.
findings.suggestion: After skipping the gap, bind a bare value using the same `_span`/`_descriptor_span` and prose/no-value guard used for unquoted labels; add tests for single- and double-quoted labels followed by whitespace and an unquoted value, including display and retained state.

findings.issue: `SENSITIVE_MARKERS` is English/Russian only. French/Spanish phrases such as `crée un projet`, `crear un proyecto`, `définir le mot de passe` or `cambiar la configuración` are not refused or pointed to explicit commands; they fall through to `say` and are sent to the engine's project agent. The explicit-action guarantee is therefore not enforced for languages the session now accepts.
findings.suggestion: Localize the sensitive-operation marker set for all supported languages, including multi-word terms, and test that these phrases never become `say` and only point to the explicit command.

findings.issue: `build_parser()` now sets a new description mentioning the interactive session, so `forgel-code --help` prints different text. The release requires every existing non-interactive usage to keep its previous output; the review's statement that `--help` is unchanged is contradicted by the diff.
findings.suggestion: Restore the previous parser description and help text, documenting the interactive mode only in README/CHANGELOG, or explicitly revise the compatibility requirement; add a `--help` output regression check if help is part of the CLI contract.

findings.issue: The README says a sentence that names no action gets a clarification, while its table and `resolve()` send an ordinary sentence to the agent as `say`; clarification is only for a task/action-shaped request with no resolvable action. The documentation is internally inconsistent.
findings.suggestion: Reword the paragraph to distinguish a plain sentence from an action request that names no available action.
